6-1.bio:
St. Justin the Philosopher and Martyr was born in Palestine and lived in the second century. Seeking truth through the schools of the philosophers, he found it at last in Christ, and thereafter wore the philosopher's cloak in the service of the Gospel. In Rome he wrote his celebrated Apologies, defending the Christians before the emperors and describing the baptism and Eucharist of the early Church.

He was beheaded in Rome with several companions around the year 165, faithful to the truth he had found. The first great Christian apologist, he is commemorated on June 1.
6-1.name: Justin the Philosopher

6-1.bio:
The companions of Saint Justin the Philosopher were arrested with him in Rome under the prefect Rusticus during the reign of Marcus Aurelius. Among them was the virgin Charito and the layman Chariton, together with Evelpistus, Hierax, Paeon, Liberian and a second Justus.

The acts of their trial survive and show each confessing Christ simply and without fear. All were beheaded together, and the Church honours them on the same day as their teacher.
6-1.desc: Holy Martyrs Justus, Chariton, Charito the virgin, Evelpistus, Hierax, Paeon and Liberian, who suffered at Rome with Justin the Philosopher.
6-1.name: Chariton, Charito and Companions, Martyrs with Justin

6-1.bio: Saint Thespesios was a Christian of Cappadocia who confessed Christ before the governor during the reign of Alexander Severus in the third century. Tradition relates that he was subjected to various tortures and finally beheaded, receiving the crown of martyrdom.
6-1.desc: Holy Martyr Thespesios of Cappadocia, who suffered for Christ under Alexander Severus.
6-1.name: Thespesios the Martyr

6-1.bio:
Saint Justin Popovich (1894-1979) was a Serbian priest-monk, professor of dogmatic theology and one of the great Orthodox theologians of the twentieth century. Removed from the university by the communist authorities, he spent his last decades confined to the women's monastery of Chelije near Valjevo, where he wrote his multi-volume Lives of the Saints and many theological works.

He was glorified by the Serbian Orthodox Church in 2010. His memory is kept on 1 June, the day of his repose according to the Julian reckoning, and he is honoured throughout the Orthodox world as a confessor and teacher.
6-1.desc: Venerable Justin Popovich, Serbian theologian and confessor of the twentieth century, spiritual father of the Chelije monastery.
6-1.name: Justin Popovich of Chelije

6-1.bio: Saint Dionysius of Glushitsa was a fifteenth-century Russian monastic who founded several monasteries in the forests of Vologda, in the region known as the Northern Thebaid. He was renowned as a strict ascetic, a painter of icons and a father to many disciples, and he reposed in 1437.
6-1.desc: Venerable Dionysius, Abbot of Glushitsa in Vologda, ascetic and iconographer of the Russian north.
6-1.name: Dionysius of Glushitsa

6-1.bio:
Saint Agapitus was a monk of the Kiev Caves Lavra in the eleventh century, a disciple of Saint Anthony of Kiev. He tended the sick of the monastery and of the city with prayer and humble remedies, asking no payment, and so received the title of Unmercenary Physician.

Tradition relates that an Armenian physician who had mocked him was converted by witnessing his healings and later became a monk himself. His relics rest in the Near Caves of Kiev.
6-1.desc: Venerable Agapitus, the unmercenary physician of the Kiev Caves, who healed the sick freely by prayer and simple herbs.
6-1.name: Agapitus of the Kiev Caves

6-1.bio: Saint Pyrrhus is remembered in the synaxaria as a bishop who preserved virginity throughout his life and shepherded his flock in holiness. Little else of his life has been preserved, and he is honoured simply as a saintly hierarch who reposed in peace.
6-1.desc: Saint Pyrrhus the Virgin, a bishop remembered for his purity of life.
6-1.name: Pyrrhus the Virgin, Bishop

6-10.bio:
The Holy Hieromartyr Timothy was Bishop of Prusa in Bithynia in the fourth century, a shepherd of holy life to whom tradition ascribes the grace of wonderworking. In the days of Julian the Apostate, when the emperor sought to restore the worship of idols, Timothy would not cease preaching Christ, and for his boldness he was imprisoned and put to death.

The Church honors him among the hieromartyrs who withstood the last pagan reaction of the empire, faithful shepherds who chose death over silence. He is commemorated on June 10.
6-10.name: Timothy, Bishop of Prusa

6-10.bio: Saint Antonina was a Christian virgin who, tradition relates, was condemned to a house of shame for refusing to sacrifice to idols. The soldier Alexander, moved by God, exchanged clothes with her so that she might escape, and when this was discovered both were tortured and burned together, in the early fourth century.
6-10.desc: Holy Martyrs Antonina the virgin and Alexander the soldier, who suffered together at Constantinople.
6-10.name: Alexander and Antonina, Martyrs

6-10.bio: Saint Neaniskos was a young Christian of Alexandria renowned for wisdom, who confessed Christ before the governor during the persecution of Diocletian. Tradition relates that he was tortured and beheaded, having proclaimed the faith with great eloquence.
6-10.desc: Holy Martyr Neaniskos the Most Wise of Alexandria, who suffered under Diocletian.
6-10.name: Neaniskos the Martyr

6-10.bio: Saint Kanides was born in Cappadocia in the time of the emperor Theodosius the Great to pious parents. From his youth he withdrew to a cave, where tradition relates he lived many decades in fasting and prayer, eating only raw vegetables, and reposed in peace at a great age.
6-10.desc: Venerable Kanides of Cappadocia, a hermit who lived from youth in a cave.
6-10.name: Kanides of Cappadocia

6-10.bio:
Saint Theophanes was a young man of Antioch who, after being widowed, gave himself to the ascetic life outside the city. Learning of a harlot named Pansemne, he sought her out, gave her money and, tradition relates, persuaded her to abandon her life and follow Christ.

Pansemne lived in repentance and asceticism near him, and both reposed in the fourth century, honoured together by the Church.
6-10.desc: Venerable Theophanes of Antioch and Pansemne, the former harlot whom he brought to repentance.
6-10.name: Theophanes and Pansemne of Antioch

6-10.bio:
Saint John was born in 1651 near Nezhin in Ukraine, became a monk of the Kiev Caves and served as archbishop of Chernigov before being sent to Tobolsk in Siberia in 1711. There he sent missionaries to the native peoples and to China, wrote spiritual works and cared generously for the poor.

He reposed in 1715 and was glorified in 1916. Saint John of Shanghai and San Francisco was his descendant and took his name.
6-10.desc: Saint John Maximovitch, Metropolitan of Tobolsk and all Siberia, missionary and wonderworker.
6-10.name: John of Tobolsk

6-10.bio: Saint Silvanus was a schemamonk of the Far Caves of the Kiev Lavra in the thirteenth or fourteenth century. Tradition relates that thieves who came to rob the monastery garden were held fast by his prayer until they repented. His relics rest in the Far Caves.
6-10.desc: Venerable Silvanus the schemamonk of the Kiev Far Caves.
6-10.name: Silvanus of the Kiev Caves

6-11.bio:
Saint Bartholomew, one of the Twelve, is generally identified with Nathanael of Cana. Tradition relates that he preached in Arabia, India and Armenia, where he was flayed and crucified for Christ.

Saint Barnabas, a Levite of Cyprus, was one of the Seventy, the companion of the Apostle Paul on his first missionary journey and the founder of the Church of Cyprus, where he was martyred at Salamis. His relics, found with the Gospel of Matthew on his breast, secured the independence of the Cypriot Church.
6-11.desc: Holy Apostles Bartholomew of the Twelve and Barnabas of the Seventy, founder of the Church of Cyprus.
6-11.name: Bartholomew and Barnabas the Apostles

6-11.bio:
Saint Luke, born Valentin Voino-Yasenetsky in 1877, was a distinguished surgeon and professor of medicine who was ordained priest and then bishop during the Soviet persecution. He spent eleven years in prisons and exile, yet continued to operate on the sick and to write, and was awarded for his surgical work during the war.

As archbishop of Simferopol he served until his repose in 1961. Glorified in 1996, he is greatly loved in Greece, where his relics and countless healings have made him one of the most venerated saints of our time.
6-11.desc: Saint Luke, Archbishop of Simferopol and Crimea, surgeon, confessor and wonderworker of the twentieth century.
6-11.name: Luke of Simferopol, the Surgeon

6-11.bio:
Saint Metrophanes was the first Chinese priest of the Russian mission in Peking. During the Boxer Rebellion in June 1900 he and his family, together with more than two hundred Orthodox Chinese, were killed for refusing to renounce Christ.

His wife Tatiana, his sons Isaiah and John and the catechist Paul Wang are commemorated with him. They were glorified in 1902 and are honoured as the first martyrs of the Chinese Church.
6-11.desc: Hieromartyr Metrophanes Chi-Sung, first Chinese Orthodox priest, with his wife Tatiana and the 222 martyrs of Peking in 1900.
6-11.name: Metrophanes of China and the Martyrs of the Boxer Rebellion

6-11.bio: Saint Barnabas lived the ascetic life in the region of Vasa near Limassol in Cyprus and is honoured there as a wonderworker. His memory is kept on the feast of the Apostle Barnabas, and a church in his name marks the place of his struggles.
6-11.desc: Venerable Barnabas the wonderworker of Vasa near Limassol, an ascetic of Cyprus.
6-11.name: Barnabas of Vasa, the Wonderworker

6-11.bio: Saint Zapheirios is commemorated in the Greek synaxaria as a New Martyr who gave his life for Christ during the years of Ottoman rule. Few details of his life have been preserved, but Greeks named Zafeiris and Zafeiria keep their name day on this feast.
6-11.desc: New Martyr Zapheirios, who confessed Christ during the Turkish period.
6-11.name: Zapheirios the New Martyr

6-12.bio:
St. Onuphrios the Great was one of the greatest hermits of the Egyptian desert, living in the fourth century. Leaving his monastery for the inner wilderness, he dwelt alone for some sixty years in utter poverty, unseen by men, clothed only in his own hair and a girdle of leaves, sustained by God in prayer.

Near the end of his life he was discovered by the monk Paphnutios, who heard his story, witnessed his blessed repose, and made his life known to the Church. He is loved as an image of total surrender to God, and is commemorated on June 12.
6-12.name: Onuphrios the Great

6-12.bio:
Saint Peter was a Byzantine soldier taken captive by the Arabs who, tradition relates, was freed through the prayers of Saint Nicholas and vowed to become a monk. Directed by a vision of the Theotokos, he went to Mount Athos in the ninth century and lived there in a cave for many decades in complete solitude.

He is honoured as the first hermit of the Holy Mountain, and his life was written by Saint Gregory Palamas.
6-12.desc: Venerable Peter the Athonite, first known hermit of the Holy Mountain.
6-12.name: Peter the Athonite

6-12.bio: Saint Antonina was a Christian virgin of Nicaea in Bithynia who confessed Christ before the governor during the persecution of Diocletian. Tradition relates that she endured many tortures and was finally drowned, sewn into a sack and cast into a lake.
6-12.desc: Holy Virgin Martyr Antonina of Nicaea, who suffered under Diocletian.
6-12.name: Antonina of Nicaea

6-12.bio: Saint Arsenius was a coppersmith of Novgorod who became a monk and spent three years on Mount Athos. Returning with an icon of the Theotokos, he founded a monastery on the island of Konevets in Lake Ladoga in the late fourteenth century and reposed there in 1447.
6-12.desc: Venerable Arsenius, founder of the Konevets monastery on Lake Ladoga.
6-12.name: Arsenius of Konevets

6-12.bio: The synaxaria of Thessaloniki commemorate the monks Synesios, Benedict and Timothy as New Martyrs who were put to death in that city during the Turkish period for their confession of Christ. Together with the monk Paul of Ioannina they are honoured on this day.
6-12.desc: Monk-Martyrs Synesios, Benedict and Timothy, monastics put to death in Thessaloniki.
6-12.name: Synesios, Benedict and Timothy, Monk-Martyrs of Thessaloniki

6-12.bio: Saint Zeno is remembered in the Greek synaxaria as a monastic who lived the ascetic life and reposed in peace. The details of his life have not been preserved.
6-12.desc: Venerable Zeno, an ascetic whose memory is preserved in the synaxaria.
6-12.name: Zeno the Venerable

6-13.bio:
The Holy Martyr Aquilina was a young girl of Byblos in Phoenicia who suffered under the persecution of Diocletian at the end of the third century. Raised in the faith from infancy, she spoke of Christ to her companions with such boldness that she was denounced to the authorities, and though only a child she endured torments and death rather than deny the Lord.

The Church honors in her the courage of the young, whose purity of faith puts the mighty to shame. She is commemorated on June 13.
6-13.name: Aquilina

6-13.bio:
Saint Triphyllius was born in Constantinople and educated in law at Beirut before becoming a disciple of Saint Spyridon of Trimythous, whose humility he learned to imitate. He was made bishop of Leucosia and was renowned for his eloquence and learning.

Saint Jerome praised him as one of the most eloquent men of his time. He reposed in peace in the fourth century.
6-13.desc: Saint Triphyllius, Bishop of Leucosia (Nicosia) in Cyprus, disciple of Saint Spyridon.
6-13.name: Triphyllius of Leucosia

6-13.bio: Saint Antipater was bishop of Bostra in Arabia in the fifth century, a contemporary of the emperor Leo. He was noted for his learning and wrote works against the errors of Origen, which were cited with approval at the later councils. He reposed in peace.
6-13.desc: Saint Antipater, Bishop of Bostra in Arabia, theologian and opponent of Origenism.
6-13.name: Antipater of Bostra

6-13.bio: Saint Anna was a widow of Constantinople who, after her husband's death, took her young son John and withdrew to a monastery, where she lived disguised as the monk Euphemianos. Tradition relates that her holiness was revealed only at her repose, and that her son also lived the monastic life in holiness.
6-13.desc: Venerable Anna of Constantinople and her son John, who lived as ascetics in the ninth century.
6-13.name: Anna and her son John of Constantinople

6-13.bio: Saint Alexandra, in the world Agatha Melgunova, was a wealthy widow who, guided by a vision of the Theotokos, founded a community of nuns at Diveyevo near Sarov in the eighteenth century. She was known to Saint Seraphim of Sarov, who later cared for the convent, and she reposed in 1789.
6-13.desc: Venerable Alexandra, foundress and first abbess of the Diveyevo convent.
6-13.name: Alexandra of Diveyevo

6-13.bio: Saint Philotheos came from the village of Sklataina near Trikala in Thessaly. In the sixteenth century he founded a monastery in the region, where he led his brethren in the ascetic life and reposed in peace. His memory is kept locally with great devotion.
6-13.desc: Venerable Philotheos of Sklataina in Thessaly, founder of a monastery near Trikala.
6-13.name: Philotheos of Sklataina

6-14.bio:
The Holy Prophet Elisha lived in the ninth century before Christ. Called from the plough by the Prophet Elijah, he left all to follow him, and when Elijah was taken up in the fiery chariot Elisha received his mantle and a double portion of his spirit. He prophesied in Israel for many years, working great wonders: healing the waters, multiplying the widow's oil, cleansing Naaman the leper, and raising the dead.

The Church honors him among the greatest of the prophets, a man of God through whom the power of the Lord was shown to a wayward people. He is commemorated on June 14.
6-14.name: Eliseos the Prophet

6-14.bio:
Saint Methodius was born in Syracuse in Sicily and became a monk and later a leading defender of the icons under the iconoclast emperors. He was imprisoned for years in a tomb-like cell and endured harsh treatment.

After the death of the emperor Theophilus he was made patriarch in 843 and, with the empress Theodora, restored the veneration of the icons. The first Sunday of Great Lent, the Sunday of Orthodoxy, was instituted under him. He reposed in 847.
6-14.desc: Saint Methodius the Confessor, Patriarch of Constantinople, who restored the holy icons and established the Sunday of Orthodoxy.
6-14.name: Methodius the Confessor, Patriarch of Constantinople

6-14.bio: Saint Cyril was bishop of Gortyna in Crete and, tradition relates, was already very old when he was arrested during the persecution of Diocletian. Condemned to be burned, he was preserved unharmed and was then beheaded, receiving the crown of martyrdom.
6-14.desc: Hieromartyr Cyril, Bishop of Gortyna in Crete, beheaded in extreme old age.
6-14.name: Cyril of Gortyna

6-14.bio: Saint Niphon was the son of a priest from Lukovo in Epirus and became a monk on Mount Athos in the fourteenth century. He lived in the wilderness of Kapsokalyvia as a companion of Saint Maximos the Hutburner and was renowned for his strict asceticism and gifts of foresight. He reposed in 1411.
6-14.desc: Venerable Niphon of Kapsokalyvia on Mount Athos, hermit and disciple of Saint Maximos the Hutburner.
6-14.name: Niphon of Athos

6-14.bio: Saint Julitta is remembered in the Greek synaxaria as a woman who lived the ascetic life and reposed in peace. The details of her life have not been preserved.
6-14.desc: Venerable Julitta, an ascetic whose memory is kept in the synaxaria.
6-14.name: Julitta the Venerable

6-15.bio:
The Holy Prophet Amos was a shepherd and dresser of sycamore trees from Tekoa, called by God in the eighth century before Christ to prophesy to the northern kingdom of Israel. A plain man with no schooling of the prophets, he spoke fearlessly against the injustice of the rich and the emptiness of worship without righteousness, declaring the word of the Lord: let justice roll down like waters.

His book stands among the twelve minor prophets, and the Church honors him as a voice of God's righteousness. He is commemorated on June 15.
6-15.name: Amos the Prophet

6-15.bio:
Saint Jerome was born in Stridon in Dalmatia around 347 and studied in Rome. After years of asceticism in the Syrian desert he settled in Bethlehem, where he lived in a monastery near the cave of the Nativity and produced his Latin translation of the Scriptures and many commentaries.

He reposed in 420. Greek men named Ieronymos keep their name day on this feast.
6-15.desc: Venerable Jerome of Stridon, ascetic of Bethlehem and translator of the Scriptures.
6-15.name: Jerome of Stridon

6-15.bio:
Saint Augustine was born in Tagaste in North Africa in 354 to the pious Monica. After years of wandering in error he was converted through the preaching of Saint Ambrose and was baptised in Milan in 387. He became bishop of Hippo and wrote the Confessions, the City of God and many other works.

He reposed in 430 during the siege of his city by the Vandals. Greek men named Avgoustinos keep their name day on this feast.
6-15.desc: Saint Augustine, Bishop of Hippo in North Africa, great teacher of the Western Church.
6-15.name: Augustine of Hippo

6-15.bio: Fortunatus, Achaicus and Stephanas are mentioned by the Apostle Paul in his first letter to the Corinthians as those who came to him from Corinth and refreshed his spirit. Stephanas and his household were the first converts of Achaia. The Church numbers them among the Seventy Apostles.
6-15.desc: Holy Apostles of the Seventy Fortunatus, Achaicus and Stephanas, co-workers of the Apostle Paul at Corinth.
6-15.name: Fortunatus, Achaicus and Stephanas the Apostles

6-15.bio: Saint Dulas was a Christian of Praetoriada in Cilicia who was arrested during the persecution under Maximian. Tradition relates that he endured many tortures before the governor and died on the way to further punishment, receiving the crown of martyrdom.
6-15.desc: Holy Martyr Dulas of Cilicia, who suffered under Maximian.
6-15.name: Dulas of Cilicia

6-15.bio:
Saint Savvas was born in Thessaloniki in the late thirteenth century and became a monk of Vatopedi on Mount Athos. He travelled to the Holy Land and lived for many years as a fool for Christ, keeping silence for two decades, before returning to Athos.

He was a counsellor of emperors and patriarchs yet refused the patriarchal throne. His life was written by his disciple Saint Philotheos Kokkinos. He reposed around 1349.
6-15.desc: Venerable Savvas of Vatopedi, the fool for Christ, ascetic of Mount Athos and the Holy Land.
6-15.name: Savvas of Vatopedi, Fool for Christ

6-15.bio: Saint Jonah was born near Galich and entered the monastic life at twelve. He became bishop of Ryazan and in 1448 was chosen metropolitan of Moscow, the first to be installed by the Russian bishops themselves. He was known for his defence of Orthodoxy and for miracles of healing, and reposed in 1461.
6-15.desc: Saint Jonah, Metropolitan of Moscow and all Russia, wonderworker.
6-15.name: Jonah, Metropolitan of Moscow

6-16.bio:
St. Tychon was Bishop of Amathus in Cyprus in the fifth century. The son of a baker, he was known from youth for his generosity to the poor, and as bishop he labored with apostolic zeal to turn the remaining pagans of the island from their idols to Christ, shepherding his flock with gentleness and prayer.

He was glorified as a wonderworker both in life and after his repose, and has been venerated in Cyprus from ancient times as one of the island's own saints. He is commemorated on June 16.
6-16.name: Tychon of Amathus

6-16.bio: Saint Mark was bishop of Apollonias and, tradition relates, was arrested for his confession of Christ, tortured and put to death, receiving the crown of martyrdom as a hierarch.
6-16.desc: Hieromartyr Mark, Bishop of Apollonias, who suffered for Christ.
6-16.name: Mark of Apollonias

6-16.bio: Saint Mnemonius was bishop of Amathus in Cyprus in the fifth century and ordained Saint Tychon, who succeeded him in that see. He is remembered as a holy hierarch who reposed in peace, and his memory is kept on the feast of his disciple.
6-16.desc: Saint Mnemonius, Bishop of Amathus in Cyprus, predecessor of Saint Tychon.
6-16.name: Mnemonius of Amathus

6-16.bio: The Forty Martyrs of Rome are remembered in the synaxaria as Christians who confessed Christ during the persecutions and were put to death by the sword. The details of their contest have not been preserved.
6-16.desc: Holy Forty Martyrs of Rome, who suffered for Christ by the sword.
6-16.name: Forty Martyrs of Rome

6-16.bio: These five Christians confessed Christ at Nicomedia during the persecutions and, tradition relates, were put to death by fire. The synaxaria honour them together on this day.
6-16.desc: Holy Five Martyrs who suffered for Christ at Nicomedia.
6-16.name: Five Martyrs of Nicomedia

6-17.bio:
The Holy Martyr Isauros, a deacon, suffered for Christ in the early centuries of the Church together with a company of fellow believers. Refusing to deny the Lord, they strengthened one another in prison and went together to their deaths, sealing their confession with their blood.

The synaxaria preserve little more of their story, but the Church keeps their memory among the companies of martyrs who stood side by side in the hour of trial. They are commemorated on June 17.
6-17.name: Isauros and companions

6-17.bio:
Saints Manuel, Sabel and Ismael were three brothers of noble Persian family who had been raised as Christians by their mother. Sent as envoys to the emperor Julian the Apostate, they refused to take part in his pagan sacrifices at Chalcedon.

Julian had them tortured and beheaded in 362, in violation of their status as ambassadors. Tradition relates that Julian's death in Persia the following year was seen as a judgement for this crime. Greeks named Manolis often keep their name day on this feast.
6-17.desc: Holy Martyrs Manuel, Sabel and Ismael, Persian brothers and envoys beheaded by Julian the Apostate.
6-17.name: Manuel, Sabel and Ismael, Martyrs

6-17.bio: Saint Philonides was bishop of Kourion in Cyprus during the persecution of Diocletian. Tradition relates that, faced with the threat of violation by the persecutors, he wrapped himself in his cloak and threw himself from a height, giving his life rather than suffer dishonour, and the Church honours him as a martyr.
6-17.desc: Hieromartyr Philonides, Bishop of Kourion in Cyprus.
6-17.name: Philonides of Kourion

6-17.bio: Saint Hypatius was born in Phrygia and became a monk in Thrace before settling at the deserted monastery of Rufinianae near Chalcedon, which he restored and led for forty years. He was known for his gifts of healing and his opposition to Nestorius, and he reposed in 446.
6-17.desc: Venerable Hypatius, abbot of the monastery of Rufinianae near Chalcedon.
6-17.name: Hypatius of Rufinianae

6-17.bio: Abba Pior was an Egyptian ascetic of the fourth century who left his family as a young man and became a disciple of Saint Anthony the Great. He lived in Scetis, and his sayings and his remarkable detachment from his relatives are recorded in the histories of the desert fathers.
6-17.desc: Venerable Pior of Egypt, a desert father and disciple of Saint Anthony.
6-17.name: Pior the Venerable

6-17.bio:
Saint Alban was a citizen of Verulamium in Roman Britain who sheltered a persecuted Christian priest and was converted by him. Exchanging clothes with the priest so that he might escape, Alban was arrested in his place, confessed Christ and was beheaded, in the third or early fourth century.

The city of Saint Albans grew up around his shrine, and he is honoured as the protomartyr of Britain.
6-17.desc: Holy Martyr Alban, the first martyr of Britain, beheaded at Verulamium.
6-17.name: Alban, Protomartyr of Britain

6-18.bio:
The Holy Martyr Leontios was a soldier of Greek descent who suffered for Christ at Tripoli in Phoenicia in the early centuries of the Church. A man of courage and charity, he confessed the Lord before his accusers, and tradition tells that his steadfastness under torment brought even those sent against him to faith in Christ, so that they shared his martyrdom.

He was venerated at Tripoli from ancient times, and churches in his honor spread through the East. He is commemorated on June 18.
6-18.name: Leontios

6-18.bio: Saint Leontius came from Argos and became a monk of the monastery of Dionysiou on Mount Athos, where tradition relates that he lived for sixty years without ever leaving the monastery. He was granted the gift of foresight, and after his repose in 1605 his relics flowed with myrrh.
6-18.desc: Venerable Leontius the Myrrh-gusher of Dionysiou Monastery on Mount Athos.
6-18.name: Leontius the Athonite, Myrrh-gusher

6-18.bio: Saint Leontius served as canonarch, the leader of the chanting, at the Kiev Caves Lavra while still very young, in the fourteenth century. He died in youth, and his relics rest in the Far Caves of the Lavra.
6-18.desc: Venerable Leontius, the young canonarch of the Kiev Caves Lavra.
6-18.name: Leontius the Canonarch of the Kiev Caves

6-18.bio: Saint Aetherius is remembered in the synaxaria as a martyr who confessed Christ and was beheaded during the persecutions. The details of his contest have not been preserved.
6-18.desc: Holy Martyr Aetherius, who suffered for Christ by the sword.
6-18.name: Aetherius the Martyr

6-19.bio:
The Holy Apostle Jude, called Thaddeus, is numbered among the Twelve and is known as the Brother of the Lord, being of the household of the righteous Joseph. He wrote the short catholic epistle that bears his name, urging the faithful to contend earnestly for the faith once delivered to the saints. After Pentecost he preached the Gospel in the lands of the East, and tradition holds that he ended his labors as a martyr.

The Church honors him as apostle, kinsman of the Lord according to the flesh, and witness unto blood. He is commemorated on June 19.
6-19.desc: Holy Apostle Jude (Thaddeus), Brother of the Lord.
6-19.name: Apostle Jude, Brother of the Lord

6-19.bio:
St. John Maximovitch, Archbishop of Shanghai and San Francisco, was one of the great saints of the twentieth century. Born in Russia in 1896, he served as bishop in Shanghai, where he sheltered orphans and the poor, and later shepherded his scattered flock in Western Europe and America. A strict ascetic who served the Divine Liturgy daily, he was known even in his lifetime as a wonderworker whose prayers brought healing.

He reposed in 1966 while accompanying a wonderworking icon of the Mother of God, and his relics rest in San Francisco. Glorified in 1994, he is honored on this day as a wonderworker of the latter times.
6-19.desc: St. John Maximovitch, Wonderworker and Archbishop of Shanghai and San Francisco.
6-19.name: John Maximovitch of Shanghai

6-19.bio:
Saint Paisius was born in Egypt in the fourth century and became a disciple of Saint Pambo in Nitria together with Saint John the Short. He lived in extreme asceticism in a cave in the desert and, tradition relates, was granted visions of Christ and the gift of foreseeing the future.

He was greatly loved by the monks of Egypt, and his life was written by Saint John the Short. His relics were later taken to Pisidia.
6-19.desc: Venerable Paisius the Great of Egypt, desert father and friend of Saint John the Short.
6-19.name: Paisius the Great

6-19.bio: Saint Zosimas was a soldier from Apollonia who confessed Christ during the persecution under Trajan. Brought before the governor at Antioch in Pisidia, he endured torture and was beheaded, receiving the crown of martyrdom.
6-19.desc: Holy Martyr Zosimas the soldier, beheaded at Antioch in Pisidia under Trajan.
6-19.name: Zosimas the Soldier

6-19.bio: Saint Job became the first patriarch of Moscow in 1589, when the Russian Church received patriarchal status. He was a man of prayer and learning who laboured for the spread of the faith in Siberia. Deposed by the False Dmitry in 1605 for refusing to recognise him, he retired to the Staritsa monastery and reposed in 1607.
6-19.desc: Saint Job, first Patriarch of Moscow and all Russia.
6-19.name: Job, Patriarch of Moscow

6-19.bio: Saint Barlaam was a boyar and governor of Novgorod named Basil who founded a monastery on the river Vaga and in old age became a monk there. He reposed in 1462 and was known for his charity and the miracles at his tomb.
6-19.desc: Venerable Barlaam of Vaga, boyar of Novgorod who became a monk and founder of a monastery on the Vaga river.
6-19.name: Barlaam of Shenkursk

6-2.bio:
St. Nikephoros was Patriarch of Constantinople in the ninth century, in the days when the iconoclast heresy rose a second time. A learned man who had served the empire before taking up the monastic life, he shepherded the Church with wisdom and stood immovably for the veneration of the holy icons. For this he was driven from his throne by the emperor and spent his last years in exile, a confessor for the Orthodox faith.

His relics were later returned to Constantinople with honor, and the Church numbers him among the great defenders of the icons. He is commemorated on June 2.
6-2.desc: Patriarch of Constantinople, defender of icons.
6-2.name: Nikephoros of Constantinople

6-2.bio:
Saint Constantine was born a Muslim in Mytilene on the island of Lesbos and, tradition relates, was drawn to Christianity after being healed at a church of the Theotokos. He was baptised on Mount Athos and lived for a time as a monk.

Burning with desire to confess his faith publicly, he returned to Constantinople, where he was imprisoned, tortured and finally hanged in 1819. He is numbered among the New Martyrs of the Turkish period.
6-2.desc: New Martyr Constantine of Mytilene, a convert from Islam who confessed Christ and was hanged in Constantinople.
6-2.name: Constantine the New Martyr, former Hagarene

6-2.bio:
Saint John was a pious merchant of Trebizond who, while travelling by sea in the fourteenth century, was denounced as a Christian at the port of Asprokastro on the Black Sea. Refusing to deny Christ, he was tortured and dragged through the streets until he died.

His relics were later brought to Suceava in Moldavia, where he is greatly venerated as the protector of that land. The Greek synaxaria also commemorate him on 12 June.
6-2.desc: Great Martyr John the New of Trebizond, a merchant martyred at Asprokastro (Cetatea Alba) and later enshrined at Suceava.
6-2.name: John the New of Trebizond, Great Martyr

6-2.bio: Saint Demetrios came from Philadelphia in Asia Minor. Tradition relates that as a young man he was pressured to renounce his faith and, after a fall, returned to Christ with repentance and confessed Him openly before the Turkish judge. He was beheaded in 1657 and is counted among the New Martyrs.
6-2.desc: New Martyr Demetrios of Philadelphia in Asia Minor, beheaded for Christ in the seventeenth century.
6-2.name: Demetrios of Philadelphia, New Martyr

6-2.bio: Saint Erasmus was a bishop from Antioch who preached the Gospel widely, including in the region of Ochrid and Lychnidos in Illyria, where many were converted through his teaching. Tradition relates that he endured torture under the persecution of Diocletian and Maximian and reposed in Campania, in Italy.
6-2.desc: Hieromartyr Erasmus, bishop and preacher who enlightened the region of Ochrid and suffered under Diocletian.
6-2.name: Erasmus of Ochrid

6-2.bio:
In the year 177 the Christians of Lyons and Vienne in Gaul suffered a savage persecution described in a letter preserved by Eusebius. The aged bishop Pothinus died in prison from his injuries, while the deacon Sanctus, the slave girl Blandina, the young Ponticus, Alcibiades, Vettius Epagathus and many others were tortured and put to death in the amphitheatre.

Blandina in particular became famous for her endurance and her encouragement of the others. The Greek synaxaria commemorate this whole company on 2 June.
6-2.desc: Hieromartyr Pothinus, Bishop of Lyons, with Blandina, Sanctus, Alcibiades, Vettius Epagathus and the other martyrs of Lyons under Marcus Aurelius.
6-2.greek: Ποθεινός και οι εν Λουγδούνω Μάρτυρες
6-2.name: Pothinus and the Martyrs of Lyons

6-2.bio: Saints Marcellinus, a priest, and Peter, an exorcist, were imprisoned at Rome during the persecution of Diocletian. Tradition relates that they converted their jailer and his household while in prison. They were led out to a wood and beheaded there in secret, and were later greatly honoured in Rome.
6-2.desc: Holy Martyrs Marcellinus the priest and Peter the exorcist, beheaded at Rome under Diocletian.
6-2.name: Marcellinus and Peter of Rome

6-20.bio:
The Holy Hieromartyr Methodius was Bishop of Patara in Lycia at the turn of the fourth century. A learned shepherd and one of the notable church writers of his age, he defended the resurrection of the body and the purity of the faith, and composed works in praise of virginity. In the last great persecution he was seized for his confession of Christ and put to death by the sword.

The Church honors him as a teacher who served the truth with both pen and blood. He is commemorated on June 20.
6-20.name: Methodius, Bishop of Patara

6-20.bio:
Saint Nicholas Cabasilas was born in Thessaloniki around 1322, a nephew of Archbishop Neilos Cabasilas. A learned layman close to the emperor John Kantakouzenos, he wrote The Life in Christ and the Commentary on the Divine Liturgy, works of great depth on the sacraments.

He was a friend of the hesychasts and of Saint Gregory Palamas, and he reposed at the end of the fourteenth century. He was formally numbered among the saints in 1983.
6-20.desc: Saint Nicholas Cabasilas of Thessaloniki, lay theologian and author of The Life in Christ.
6-20.name: Nicholas Cabasilas

6-20.bio: Saint Callistus was a monk of Mount Athos and a disciple of Saint Gregory of Sinai. He became patriarch of Constantinople in 1350 and again in 1355, presided over the council that confirmed the teaching of Saint Gregory Palamas, and wrote lives of the saints and spiritual works. He reposed in Serres in 1363 while on an embassy to the Serbs.
6-20.desc: Saint Callistus I, Patriarch of Constantinople, hesychast of Mount Athos and disciple of Saint Gregory of Sinai.
6-20.name: Callistus I, Patriarch of Constantinople

6-20.bio: Saint Athanasius lived the ascetic life at Pentaschoinon near Larnaca in Cyprus and is honoured there as a wonderworker. Tradition relates that he was an obedient youth who died young and was revealed as a saint through miracles at his tomb, where a church was built in his name.
6-20.desc: Venerable Athanasius the wonderworker of Pentaschoinon in Cyprus.
6-20.name: Athanasius of Pentaschoinon

6-21.bio:
Saint Julian was a young man of Tarsus in Cilicia, of a senatorial family, who was arrested during the persecution of Diocletian. Tradition relates that he was dragged from city to city for a year to break his resolve and finally sewn into a sack with vipers and drowned in the sea.

His mother followed him and encouraged him to the end. Saint John Chrysostom preached a homily in his honour, and his relics were venerated at Antioch.
6-21.desc: Holy Martyr Julian of Tarsus, cast into the sea in a sack of vipers under Diocletian.
6-21.name: Julian of Tarsus

6-21.bio: Saint Terence was bishop of Iconium in Lycaonia. Tradition relates that he was arrested for preaching Christ, endured torture and was beheaded, receiving the crown of martyrdom.
6-21.desc: Hieromartyr Terence, Bishop of Iconium, who suffered for Christ.
6-21.name: Terence of Iconium

6-21.bio:
Saint Niketas was born on the island of Nisyros to a Christian family that had been forced to embrace Islam. Learning of his origins, he fled to Chios, was received back into the Church and lived for a time at the monastery of Nea Moni.

Desiring martyrdom, he confessed Christ before the Turkish judge in Chios and was beheaded there in 1732.
6-21.desc: New Martyr Niketas of Nisyros, beheaded on Chios in 1732.
6-21.name: Niketas of Nisyros

6-21.bio: Saint Anastasia, in the world Anna, was the wife of the Serbian ruler Stefan Nemanja and the mother of Saint Sava and of Saint Stefan the First-Crowned. After her husband became the monk Symeon she also took monastic vows and lived in prayer until her repose, around 1200.
6-21.desc: Venerable Anastasia of Serbia, wife of Stefan Nemanja and mother of Saint Sava.
6-21.name: Anastasia of Serbia

6-22.bio:
St. Eusebios, Bishop of Samosata, was one of the great champions of the Nicene faith in the fourth century, a friend and fellow struggler of St. Basil the Great. In the years when Arianism held the empire, he traveled through the East, tradition says even in disguise, strengthening the faithful and ordaining Orthodox clergy, and for this he was driven into exile under the emperor Valens.

Returning after the persecution eased, he met a martyr's end around the year 380, struck down by a tile hurled by a woman of the heretics as he entered a city to install an Orthodox bishop. He is commemorated on June 22.
6-22.name: Eusebios of Samosata

6-22.bio: Saint Zeno was a wealthy Christian of Philadelphia in Arabia who freed his slaves and gave away his goods. When he rebuked the governor for persecuting Christians he was arrested, and his former servant Zenas, refusing to leave him, shared his imprisonment. Both were beheaded in the early fourth century.
6-22.desc: Holy Martyrs Zeno and his servant Zenas of Philadelphia in Arabia, beheaded under Maximian.
6-22.name: Zeno and Zenas of Philadelphia

6-22.bio: Saint Galaction, tradition relates, was drowned for his confession of Christ, while Saint Juliana and her son Saturninus were burned. The synaxaria commemorate them together as martyrs of Constantinople.
6-22.desc: Holy Martyrs Galaction, and Juliana with her son Saturninus, who suffered at Constantinople.
6-22.name: Galaction, Juliana and Saturninus

6-22.bio:
Saint Gregory, called the Teacher, was a monk of Neamts formed in the tradition of Saint Paisius Velichkovsky, and devoted himself to translating the writings of the Fathers into Romanian. He became metropolitan of Wallachia in 1823, laboured for the education of clergy and the care of the poor, and endured exile for his defence of the Church.

He reposed in 1834 and was glorified by the Romanian Orthodox Church in 2006.
6-22.desc: Saint Gregory Dascalul, Metropolitan of Wallachia, translator of the Fathers and disciple of the tradition of Saint Paisius Velichkovsky.
6-22.name: Gregory the Teacher, Metropolitan of Wallachia

6-23.bio:
The Holy Martyr Agrippina was a Christian maiden of Rome who suffered for Christ in the third century. Raised in piety, she adorned herself not with gold but with chastity and prayer, and when persecution came she confessed the Lord openly and died under torture rather than deny Him.

Her holy relics were carried by devout women to Sicily, where her veneration flourished from ancient times and many miracles were ascribed to her intercession. She is commemorated on June 23.
6-23.name: Agrippina

6-23.bio: Saint Aristocles was a priest of Tamassos in Cyprus who, tradition relates, was called by a heavenly voice to go to Salamis and confess Christ. He was joined by the deacon Demetrian and the reader Athanasius. All three were arrested and beheaded there in the early fourth century, under Maximian.
6-23.desc: Holy Martyrs Aristocles the priest, Demetrian the deacon and Athanasius the reader, beheaded at Salamis in Cyprus.
6-23.name: Aristocles, Demetrian and Athanasius, Martyrs of Cyprus

6-23.bio: Saint Eustochius was a pagan priest who, witnessing the courage of the Christian martyrs, was converted and later ordained priest at Antioch. He brought his nephew Gaius and the children Probus, Lollius and Urban to the faith, and all were arrested at Ancyra in Galatia and put to death under Maximian.
6-23.desc: Holy Martyrs Eustochius the priest, his nephew Gaius, and the children Probus, Lollius and Urban, who suffered at Ancyra.
6-23.name: Eustochius, Gaius, Probus, Lollius and Urban of Ancyra

6-23.bio:
In June 1821, at the outbreak of the Greek revolution, the Ottoman authorities in Heraklion put to death Metropolitan Gerasimos of Crete and the bishops of Knossos, Chersonissos, Lampi, Sitia, Petra, Rethymno, Kydonia, Kissamos and Diopolis, together with many priests, monks and lay people, in the cathedral of Saint Menas and elsewhere on the island.

The Church honours them together as the hieromartyrs of Crete on this day.
6-23.desc: Holy Hieromartyrs Gerasimos, Metropolitan of Crete, and the bishops Neophytos, Joachim, Hierotheos, Zacharias, Kallinikos and Melchisedek, with the clergy and laity slain in 1821 and 1822.
6-23.greek: Γεράσιμος Κρήτης και οι συν αυτώ
6-23.name: Hieromartyrs of Crete, Gerasimos of Crete and Companions

6-23.bio: Saint Barbarus, tradition relates, was a brigand who came to repentance and spent years in severe penance, living among the animals in the mountains. He was killed by hunters who mistook him for a wild beast, and his relics, venerated in western Greece, became a source of healing. The synaxaria also commemorate him in May.
6-23.desc: Venerable Barbarus the former brigand, ascetic and wonderworker of Pentapolis.
6-23.name: Barbarus of Pentapolis

6-23.bio: Saint Etheldreda was a princess of East Anglia who, though twice married, preserved her virginity and finally received the monastic habit. She founded the monastery of Ely and served as its abbess until her repose in 679. Her relics were found incorrupt, and her shrine at Ely was one of the great pilgrimage places of England.
6-23.desc: Venerable Etheldreda (Audrey), queen and abbess of Ely in England.
6-23.name: Etheldreda of Ely

6-24.bio:
The Nativity of St. John the Forerunner is celebrated on June 24, six months before the Nativity of Christ. The Gospel of Luke recounts how the Archangel Gabriel announced to the aged priest Zacharias that his barren wife Elizabeth would bear a son; struck mute for his doubt, Zacharias regained his speech at the naming of the child and prophesied that the boy would be called the prophet of the Most High.

John was born to prepare the way of the Lord, and his birth was itself the beginning of the joy of the Gospel. The Church keeps the feast as one of the great celebrations of the Forerunner.
6-24.desc: Nativity of the Holy Forerunner and Baptist John.
6-24.name: Nativity of John the Baptist

6-24.bio:
Saint Athanasius was born on Paros in 1721 and studied in Smyrna and at the Athonite Academy under Eugenios Voulgaris. He taught in Thessaloniki, Corfu and Chios and, with Saints Nikodemos the Hagiorite and Makarios of Corinth, was a leader of the Kollyvades renewal that called for frequent communion and fidelity to the tradition of the Fathers.

He reposed on Chios in 1813 and was glorified in 1995.
6-24.desc: Venerable Athanasius Parios, theologian and teacher, leading figure of the Kollyvades movement.
6-24.name: Athanasius Parios

6-24.bio: On the day after the Nativity of the Forerunner the Church remembers his parents, the priest Zacharias and Elizabeth, kinswoman of the Theotokos. Barren until old age, they received the promise of a son from the archangel Gabriel, and Zacharias, struck dumb for his doubt, prophesied at the child's naming. Their principal feast is kept on 5 September.
6-24.desc: Synaxis of the Righteous Zacharias and Elizabeth, parents of Saint John the Baptist.
6-24.name: Righteous Zacharias and Elizabeth

6-24.bio:
Saint Panagiotis was born in Caesarea of Cappadocia and worked as a young man in Constantinople. Tradition relates that he was falsely accused of insulting the Muslim faith and, refusing to save his life by conversion, confessed Christ boldly and was beheaded in 1765.

Men named Panagiotis, who usually keep their name day on the Dormition, may also honour this New Martyr on his feast.
6-24.desc: New Martyr Panagiotis of Caesarea in Cappadocia, beheaded in Constantinople in 1765.
6-24.name: Panagiotis of Caesarea, New Martyr

6-25.bio:
St. Febronia was a young nun of Mesopotamia who suffered for Christ at the beginning of the fourth century, in the persecution of Diocletian. Raised in a monastery from childhood, she was famed for her beauty, her wisdom, and her love of the Scriptures. When the persecutors seized her, she refused the offer of marriage and freedom in exchange for denying Christ, and endured a cruel martyrdom with unbroken faith.

Her contest, recorded by the nuns who knew her, made her one of the most venerated virgin-martyrs of the East. She is commemorated on June 25.
6-25.name: Febronia

6-25.bio:
Saint Dionysius was born near Kastoria in the fourteenth century and went to Mount Athos, where his brother Theodosius was a monk. Guided, tradition relates, by a light he saw on a rock above the sea, he founded there the monastery of the Holy Forerunner, later known by his name, with the support of the emperor Alexios III of Trebizond.

He reposed in Trebizond around 1388 while seeking help for his monastery.
6-25.desc: Venerable Dionysius of Koritsa, founder of the monastery of the Holy Forerunner (Dionysiou) on Mount Athos.
6-25.name: Dionysius of Athos, Founder of Dionysiou

6-25.bio: Saint Procopius was born in Varna in Bulgaria and became a monk of the Iviron monastery on Mount Athos. Tradition relates that he fell into apostasy in Smyrna, but quickly repented and returned to confess Christ before the judge, and was beheaded there in 1810.
6-25.desc: Monk-Martyr Procopius of Varna and Iviron, beheaded in Smyrna in 1810.
6-25.name: Procopius of Smyrna, Monk-Martyr

6-25.bio: Saint George was born in Attaleia in Asia Minor. Tradition relates that he was raised as a Muslim after being taken from his Christian parents, but returned to the faith of Christ. Denounced at Krini opposite Chios, he confessed Christ openly and was put to death in 1823.
6-25.desc: New Martyr George of Attaleia, who suffered at Krini (Cesme) in 1823.
6-25.name: George of Attaleia, New Martyr

6-25.bio: These seven brothers were soldiers in the imperial army in Thrace. When Orentius refused to sacrifice after a victory in single combat, all seven were stripped of their rank and sent in chains along the Black Sea coast toward the Caucasus, where each died in a different place of exile or by violence, in the early fourth century.
6-25.desc: Holy Martyrs Orentius, Pharnacius, Eros, Firmus, Firminus, Cyriacus and Longinus, seven brothers and soldiers who suffered under Maximian.
6-25.name: Orentius and his Six Brothers, Martyrs

6-25.bio: Saints Leonis, Libye and her young sister Eutropia were Christian women of Palmyra in Syria who confessed Christ during the persecutions. Tradition relates that Leonis was burned, Libye beheaded, and the twelve-year-old Eutropia shot with arrows.
6-25.desc: Holy Women Martyrs Leonis, Libye and Eutropia, who suffered for Christ in Syria.
6-25.name: Leonis, Libye and Eutropia, Monastic Martyrs

6-25.bio:
Saint Peter, prince of Murom, was healed of a grievous illness by the peasant maiden Fevronia and married her, and the two ruled Murom with justice and mercy in the thirteenth century. Late in life both received the monastic habit, and tradition relates that they died on the same day and were buried together.

They are honoured in Russia as patrons of marriage and family life.
6-25.desc: Righteous Prince Peter and Princess Fevronia of Murom, wonderworkers and patrons of Christian marriage.
6-25.name: Peter and Fevronia of Murom

6-26.bio:
St. David of Thessaloniki was an ascetic of the sixth century who lived in that city as a stranger to the world. Tradition tells that he made his dwelling in the branches of an almond tree, enduring heat and cold for years in prayer, until God revealed that his petition was heard; thereafter he lived in a cell, where the faithful sought his prayers and counsel, and he was granted the grace of wonderworking.

He is one of the beloved patron saints of Thessaloniki, where his relics are venerated to this day. He is commemorated on June 26.
6-26.name: David of Thessaloniki

6-26.bio: Saint John was born in Crimea and became bishop of the Goths who lived there in the eighth century. He travelled to Jerusalem and Georgia, defended the veneration of icons against the iconoclast emperors, and was imprisoned by the Khazars, from whom he escaped. He reposed in Amastris around 790.
6-26.desc: Saint John the Confessor, Bishop of the Goths in Crimea, defender of the holy icons.
6-26.name: John, Bishop of Gothia

6-26.bio: Saint David was born in Aivali in Asia Minor and became a monk at the Skete of Saint Anne on Mount Athos. Sent to Thessaloniki on monastery business, tradition relates that he was moved to confess Christ before the Turkish authorities and was hanged there in 1813.
6-26.desc: Monk-Martyr David of Aivali and Saint Anne's Skete, hanged in Thessaloniki in 1813.
6-26.name: David the New Monk-Martyr

6-26.bio: Saint Dionysius was a monk of the Kiev Caves who founded the Ascension Caves monastery at Nizhny Novgorod and became bishop of Suzdal. He was a friend of Saint Sergius of Radonezh and Saint Alexis of Moscow and was named metropolitan of Russia, but was detained in Kiev, where he reposed in 1385.
6-26.desc: Saint Dionysius, Archbishop of Suzdal, founder of the Caves monastery of Nizhny Novgorod.
6-26.name: Dionysius of Suzdal

6-26.bio: Saint Anthion is remembered in the Greek synaxaria as a monastic who lived the ascetic life and reposed in peace. The details of his life have not been preserved.
6-26.desc: Venerable Anthion, an ascetic whose memory is preserved in the synaxaria.
6-26.name: Anthion the Venerable

6-27.bio:
St. Sampson the Hospitable was a physician of noble birth who settled in Constantinople in the days of the emperor Justinian. Ordained a priest, he gave his skill and his wealth to the sick and the poor, receiving them into his own house; tradition tells that he healed the emperor himself, and with imperial help there arose the great hospice that bore his name for centuries, one of the famed houses of Christian mercy in the city.

He is honored among the unmercenary physicians, a father of Christian medicine and philanthropy. He is commemorated on June 27.
6-27.desc: Venerable Samson the Hospitable of Constantinople.
6-27.name: Sampson the Hospitable

6-27.bio:
Saint Joanna was the wife of Chuza, the steward of Herod Antipas. The Gospel of Luke names her among the women who followed Christ and ministered to Him from their means, and among the myrrhbearers who found the tomb empty on the morning of the Resurrection.

Tradition relates that she recovered the head of Saint John the Baptist after his execution and buried it with honour on the Mount of Olives. Greek women named Ioanna keep their name day on this feast.
6-27.desc: Holy Myrrhbearer Joanna, wife of Chuza the steward of Herod, who ministered to Christ and came to His tomb.
6-27.name: Joanna the Myrrhbearer

6-27.bio:
Saint Cyril Loukaris was born in Crete in 1572 and studied in Venice and Padua. He served as patriarch of Alexandria and then, several times, as patriarch of Constantinople, labouring for the education of the Orthodox and resisting Latin influence during a turbulent period.

He was strangled by the Ottoman authorities in 1638 and his body cast into the Bosphorus. He was numbered among the saints by the Patriarchate of Alexandria in 2009.
6-27.desc: Hieromartyr Cyril Loukaris, Patriarch of Alexandria and Constantinople, strangled by the Turks in 1638.
6-27.name: Cyril Loukaris, Patriarch of Constantinople

6-27.bio: Saint Anectus was a Christian of Caesarea in Cappadocia who, tradition relates, openly confessed Christ during the persecution of Diocletian, encouraged those being tortured, and was himself tortured and beheaded.
6-27.desc: Holy Martyr Anectus of Caesarea in Cappadocia, who suffered under Diocletian.
6-27.name: Anectus the Martyr

6-27.bio: Saint Luke is remembered in the Greek synaxaria as a hermit who lived the solitary ascetic life and reposed in peace. The details of his life have not been preserved.
6-27.desc: Venerable Luke the hermit, an ascetic whose memory is preserved in the synaxaria.
6-27.name: Luke the Hermit

6-27.bio: Saint Pierius was a priest of Antioch who, tradition relates, was arrested for his confession of Christ during the persecutions and gave his life as a hieromartyr.
6-27.name: Pierius of Antioch

6-28.bio:
On June 28 the Church commemorates the translation of the relics of the Holy Unmercenaries Cyrus and John. Cyrus was a physician of Alexandria who healed in the name of Christ without payment, and John a soldier who joined him; together they strengthened the confessors during the persecution of Diocletian and were beheaded for the faith at the beginning of the fourth century.

In the fifth century their relics were translated with honor to Menouthis near Alexandria, where countless healings were wrought and the last strongholds of paganism gave way. Their principal feast is kept on January 31, and the translation of their relics on June 28.
6-28.desc: Translation of the relics of the Holy Unmercenaries Cyrus and John.
6-28.name: Sts. Cyrus & John the Unmercenaries

6-28.bio: Saints Sergius and Herman are honoured as the founders of the monastery of Valaam on an island in Lake Ladoga, from which the Christian faith spread among the Karelian peoples. Tradition places them in the fourteenth century, though some accounts make them earlier, and their relics rest at Valaam.
6-28.desc: Venerable Sergius and Herman, founders of the Valaam monastery on Lake Ladoga and enlighteners of Karelia.
6-28.greek: Σέργιος και Γερμανός οι εν Βαλάμη
6-28.name: Sergius and Herman of Valaam

6-28.bio: Saint Paul was a physician of Corinth who became a monk. Tradition relates that a woman falsely accused him of fathering her child and that the infant, only days old, spoke to declare his innocence. He lived thereafter in great asceticism, gifted with healing, and reposed at an advanced age in the seventh century.
6-28.desc: Venerable Paul the physician of Corinth, ascetic falsely accused and vindicated by a miracle.
6-28.name: Paul the Physician of Corinth

6-28.bio: Saint Pappias confessed Christ during the persecution of Diocletian and, tradition relates, was tortured and put to death, receiving the crown of martyrdom.
6-28.desc: Holy Martyr Pappias, who suffered for Christ under Diocletian.
6-28.name: Pappias the Martyr

6-28.bio: Saint Sergius was a nobleman of Paphlagonia related to the empress Theodora, who held the rank of magistros in the ninth century. Tradition relates that he was exiled for his defence of the icons and that afterwards he founded a monastery of the Theotokos on his estate, where he ended his days in prayer.
6-28.desc: Righteous Sergius the Magistros of Paphlagonia, founder of a monastery of the Theotokos.
6-28.name: Sergius the Magistros

6-28.bio: The Seventy Martyrs of Scythopolis are remembered in the synaxaria as Christians who confessed Christ together during the persecutions and were put to death. The details of their contest have not been preserved.
6-28.desc: Holy Seventy Martyrs who suffered for Christ at Scythopolis in Palestine.
6-28.name: Seventy Martyrs of Scythopolis

6-29.bio:
The feast of Sts. Peter and Paul honors together the two chief Apostles. St. Peter, the fisherman of Galilee who confessed Christ as the Son of the living God, was foremost among the Twelve and, after his denial and restoration, strengthened the brethren and preached to the end. St. Paul, once a persecutor of the Church, was converted by the risen Christ on the road to Damascus and became the Apostle to the Nations.

According to tradition both were martyred in Rome under Nero, Peter by crucifixion and Paul by the sword. Their feast on June 29 crowns the Apostles Fast and is a cherished name day for Petros and Pavlos.
6-29.desc: Feast of the Chief Apostles Peter and Paul.
6-29.name: Peter and Paul the Apostles

6-29.bio: Saint Cyril is commemorated in the Greek synaxaria on this day as a martyr who gave his life for Christ. The details of his contest have not been preserved.
6-29.desc: Holy Martyr Cyril, whose memory is kept on the feast of the Apostles Peter and Paul.
6-29.name: Cyril the Martyr

6-3.bio:
The Holy Martyr Lukillian had been a pagan priest who came to faith in Christ in his old age. Baptized, he confessed the Lord openly and suffered in the third century near Byzantium, enduring torments together with young companions who would not deny Christ, and with them received the crown of martyrdom.

His conversion at the end of a long life given to idols shows that it is never too late to turn to the living God, and that grace can make even an aged newcomer a witness unto blood. He is commemorated on June 3.
6-3.name: Lukillian

6-3.bio:
Saint Paula was a Christian maiden of Byzantium who cared for the aged martyr Lucillian and the four young boys, Claudius, Hypatius, Paul and Dionysius, who were imprisoned with him under the emperor Aurelian. After the men were put to death she was arrested for her ministry to the martyrs.

Tradition relates that she was taken to Byzantium and beheaded there. Greek women named Pavlina keep their name day on her feast.
6-3.desc: Holy Virgin Martyr Paula, who suffered at Byzantium with the infants Claudius, Hypatius, Paul and Dionysius, companions of Lucillian.
6-3.name: Paula the Virgin Martyr and the Four Infants

6-3.bio:
At the outbreak of the Greek War of Independence in 1821 the Ottoman authorities executed many hierarchs of the Church in Constantinople. Metropolitan Joseph of Thessaloniki, Dorotheos Proios of Adrianople, a noted scholar, and Gregory of Derkoi were among those hanged on 3 June of that year, shortly after the martyrdom of Patriarch Gregory V.

They are honoured by the Church of Greece as hieromartyrs who gave their lives for the faith and their people.
6-3.desc: Hieromartyrs Joseph, Metropolitan of Thessaloniki, Dorotheos Proios of Adrianople and Gregory of Derkoi, hanged in Constantinople in 1821.
6-3.greek: Ιωσήφ, Δωρόθεος και Γρηγόριος οι Ιερομάρτυρες
6-3.name: Joseph of Thessaloniki, Dorotheos of Adrianople and Gregory of Derkoi, Hieromartyrs

6-3.bio:
Saint Kevin was born in Leinster in the sixth century and from his youth sought the solitary life. He settled in the valley of Glendalough, where a great monastic community gathered around him, and it became one of the chief centres of Irish monasticism.

Many traditions relate his closeness to the wild creatures and his severe asceticism. He is said to have reposed at a great age, and Glendalough remained a place of pilgrimage for centuries.
6-3.desc: Venerable Kevin, abbot and founder of the monastery of Glendalough in Ireland.
6-3.name: Kevin of Glendalough

6-3.bio: Saint Achillas was a priest and head of the catechetical school of Alexandria who succeeded the hieromartyr Peter as archbishop of that city in the early fourth century. Though his episcopate was short, he was honoured for his learning and virtue and reposed in peace.
6-3.desc: Saint Achillas, Archbishop of Alexandria, successor of the hieromartyr Peter.
6-3.name: Achillas of Alexandria

6-3.bio: Saint Clotilde, a Burgundian princess, married Clovis, king of the Franks, and by her prayers and example led him to be baptised, an event of great consequence for the Christian history of Gaul. After his death she withdrew to Tours, where she lived in prayer and works of mercy near the tomb of Saint Martin until her repose in 545.
6-3.desc: Righteous Clotilde, queen of the Franks, who brought her husband Clovis to the Christian faith.
6-3.name: Clotilde, Queen of the Franks

6-30.bio:
On the day after the feast of Sts. Peter and Paul, the Church celebrates in one synaxis the Twelve Apostles of Christ. Chosen by the Lord to be with Him and to be sent out to preach, they received the Holy Spirit at Pentecost and carried the Gospel to the ends of the known world, nearly all of them sealing their witness with martyrdom.

The Church is called apostolic because it rests upon their preaching and continues their mission. The synaxis on June 30 gathers into one commemoration the men through whom the good news of the Resurrection was first proclaimed in every land.
6-30.desc: Synaxis of the Glorious and All-Praised Twelve Apostles.
6-30.name: Synaxis of the Holy Apostles

6-30.bio: Saint Meliton is remembered in the synaxaria as a martyr who confessed Christ during the persecutions and gave his life for the faith. The details of his contest have not been preserved.
6-30.desc: Holy Martyr Meliton, who suffered for Christ.
6-30.name: Meliton the Martyr

6-30.bio: Saint Peter came from Sinope on the Black Sea and, tradition relates, was put to death for his confession of Christ. The synaxaria commemorate him on the day of the Synaxis of the Twelve Apostles.
6-30.desc: Holy Martyr Peter of Sinope, who suffered for Christ.
6-30.name: Peter of Sinope

6-30.bio: Saint Peter was a nephew of the khan of the Golden Horde who was moved by the preaching of Saint Cyril, bishop of Rostov, and received baptism. He settled in Rostov, where tradition relates that the Apostles Peter and Paul appeared to him and he founded a monastery in their honour. He took the monastic habit before his repose in 1290.
6-30.desc: Righteous Peter, prince of the Golden Horde, who was baptised and founded a monastery at Rostov.
6-30.name: Peter, Prince of the Horde

6-4.bio:
St. Metrophanes was the first hierarch of Constantinople, shepherding the Church of Byzantium in the days when St. Constantine the Great made the city his capital. A man of peace and holiness, he guided his flock through the end of the persecutions into the freedom of the Church; by reason of his great age he could not travel to the First Ecumenical Council at Nicaea, but he upheld its faith.

He reposed in peace soon after, honored by emperor and people alike, and is venerated as the first of the city's long line of archbishops. He is commemorated on June 4.
6-4.name: Metrophanes of Constantinople

6-4.bio:
Martha and Mary of Bethany received Christ in their home, and the Gospel records Martha's service and Mary's sitting at the Lord's feet, as well as their faith at the raising of their brother Lazarus. Tradition relates that after Pentecost they left Judea with Lazarus and ended their lives in Cyprus.

Greek women named Martha keep their name day on this feast.
6-4.desc: Righteous Martha and Mary of Bethany, the sisters of Lazarus, friends and disciples of the Lord.
6-4.name: Martha and Mary, Sisters of Lazarus

6-4.bio: Saint Sophia lived in Ainos in Thrace and was the mother of six children. After she was widowed and her children died, she devoted herself to prayer and to the care of orphans and the poor, becoming a mother to many. Tradition relates that she lived in great simplicity and reposed in peace in the tenth century.
6-4.desc: Venerable Sophia of Ainos in Thrace, a mother of six who became an ascetic and mother to orphans.
6-4.name: Sophia of Ainos

6-4.bio: Saint John was abbot of the monastery of Monagria near Kyzikos in the eighth century. During the iconoclast persecution he refused to renounce the veneration of the holy icons, and tradition relates that he was sewn into a sack and cast into the sea.
6-4.desc: Monk-Martyr John, abbot of the monastery of Monagria, drowned by the iconoclasts for venerating the holy icons.
6-4.name: John of Monagria, Monk-Martyr

6-4.bio: Abba Alonius was one of the Egyptian desert fathers of the fourth and fifth centuries. Several of his sayings survive in the Sayings of the Desert Fathers, including his teaching that a man cannot be at peace until he says in his heart that only he and God are in the world.
6-4.desc: Venerable Alonius of Egypt, a desert father whose sayings are preserved in the Apophthegmata.
6-4.name: Alonius the Venerable

6-4.bio: These four martyrs suffered in the early fourth century at Noviodunum, near present-day Niculitel in Romania. Their tomb, inscribed with their names, was discovered in 1971 beneath an ancient church, one of the oldest martyr shrines found in the region.
6-4.desc: Holy Martyrs Zoticus, Attalus, Kamasis and Philip, who suffered at Noviodunum in Scythia Minor.
6-4.name: Zoticus, Attalus, Kamasis and Philip of Niculitel

6-4.bio: Saint Methodius was one of the first disciples of Saint Sergius of Radonezh. With his teacher's blessing he founded a monastery on the river Peshnosha, near Dmitrov, and led it in the tradition of Saint Sergius until his repose in 1392.
6-4.desc: Venerable Methodius, abbot of Peshnosha, a disciple of Saint Sergius of Radonezh.
6-4.name: Methodius of Peshnosha

6-5.bio:
The Holy Hieromartyr Dorotheus was Bishop of Tyre in Phoenicia. He suffered exile in the great persecution under Diocletian, returned to his flock in the peace of the Church, and shepherded them for many years as a learned and holy elder. In extreme old age, tradition tells, he was seized in the days of Julian the Apostate and died a martyr from the torments inflicted on him.

The Church honors him as a shepherd who served through persecution, peace, and persecution again, faithful across a whole century of the Church's life. He is commemorated on June 5.
6-5.name: Dorotheus of Tyre

6-5.bio: Saint Mark was born in Smyrna. Tradition relates that after a moral fall he renounced his faith, but soon repented and, after preparing himself in prayer, went to Chios, where he publicly confessed Christ before the Turkish authorities. He was beheaded there on 5 June 1801.
6-5.desc: New Martyr Mark of Smyrna, beheaded on Chios in 1801 after returning to Christ with repentance.
6-5.name: Mark the New Martyr of Chios

6-5.bio: These ten Egyptian Christians confessed Christ during the persecution under Maximian and, tradition relates, were tortured and then left to die of hunger and thirst in the desert, thereby receiving the crown of martyrdom.
6-5.desc: Holy Martyrs Marcian, Nicander, Hyperechius, Apollonius, Leonides, Arius, Gorgias, Selenias, Irene and Pambo of Egypt.
6-5.name: Ten Martyrs of Egypt

6-5.bio:
Saint Boniface was an Englishman named Winfrid who left his monastery to preach the Gospel among the Germanic peoples in the eighth century. He founded churches and monasteries, including Fulda, and became archbishop of Mainz.

In old age he returned to missionary work in Frisia, where he and his companions were killed by pagans in 754. He is honoured as the enlightener of Germany.
6-5.desc: Hieromartyr Boniface, apostle of the Germans, archbishop of Mainz, slain by pagans in Frisia.
6-5.name: Boniface of Germany

6-5.bio: Prince Theodore was the elder brother of Saint Alexander Nevsky and ruled Novgorod with him as a youth. He died suddenly in 1233 on the eve of his wedding, and his incorrupt relics, discovered later, were venerated at Novgorod.
6-5.desc: Righteous Prince Theodore of Novgorod, elder brother of Saint Alexander Nevsky.
6-5.name: Theodore Yaroslavich of Novgorod

6-5.bio: Saints Christopher and Conon are remembered in the synaxaria as martyrs who suffered for Christ in Rome. The details of their contest have not been preserved beyond the record that they died by the sword for their confession.
6-5.desc: Holy Martyrs Christopher and Conon, who suffered for Christ at Rome.
6-5.name: Christopher and Conon of Rome

6-6.bio:
St. Hilarion the New was abbot of the Dalmaton monastery in Constantinople in the ninth century. A monk of strict life and deep humility, he guided his brotherhood in the ways of prayer and obedience, and when the iconoclast emperors renewed their war on the holy icons he refused to submit, enduring imprisonment and exile for the sake of the Orthodox faith.

He is honored as a confessor, one of the monastic fathers whose steadfastness preserved the veneration of the icons until its final restoration. He is commemorated on June 6.
6-6.name: Hilarion the New

6-6.bio:
Saint Bessarion was an Egyptian ascetic of the fourth and fifth centuries, a disciple of Saint Anthony and Saint Macarius. He lived as a wanderer without shelter, and the desert fathers preserved accounts of his great endurance and of the miracles God worked through him, including turning salt water sweet.

His sayings appear in the Apophthegmata, and monks named Bessarion keep his feast.
6-6.desc: Venerable Bessarion the Great, wonderworker of Egypt, a wandering ascetic of the desert.
6-6.name: Bessarion the Wonderworker

6-6.bio: Saint Attalus lived the ascetic life in the fourth century and is remembered in the synaxaria as a wonderworker who reposed in peace. Little more of his life has been recorded.
6-6.desc: Venerable Attalus the wonderworker, an ascetic of the fourth century.
6-6.name: Attalus the Wonderworker

6-6.bio: These five virgins of Caesarea in Palestine confessed Christ before the governor during the persecutions and were put to death by the sword. The synaxaria honour them together as a company of virgin martyrs.
6-6.desc: Holy Five Virgin Martyrs Martha, Mary, Kyria, Valeria and Marcia of Caesarea in Palestine.
6-6.greek: Μάρθα, Μαρία, Κυρία, Βαλερία και Μαρκία
6-6.name: Martha, Mary, Kyria, Valeria and Marcia, Virgin Martyrs

6-6.bio: Abba Anoub was an Egyptian ascetic of the fourth century who, tradition relates, confessed Christ during the persecutions and afterwards lived in the desert with his brother Abba Poemen and others. His humility is recorded in the Sayings of the Desert Fathers, and he is called Sign-bearer because of the miracles worked through him.
6-6.desc: Venerable Anoub the Sign-bearer of Egypt, a confessor and ascetic of Scetis.
6-6.name: Anoub the Sign-bearer

6-6.bio: Saint Gelasius, tradition relates, gave away his property to the poor and openly encouraged the Christians who were being persecuted, kissing their wounds. He was arrested for this and beheaded, receiving the crown of martyrdom.
6-6.desc: Holy Martyr Gelasius, who distributed his goods to the poor and was beheaded for Christ.
6-6.name: Gelasius the Martyr

6-6.bio: Saint Andronicus was archbishop of Perm in Russia and a courageous opponent of the persecution of the Church after the revolution. He was arrested and murdered in 1918 and is honoured among the New Martyrs and Confessors of Russia.
6-6.desc: Hieromartyr Andronicus, Archbishop of Perm, killed by the Bolsheviks in 1918.
6-6.name: Andronicus of Perm

6-7.bio:
The Holy Martyr Theodotus of Ancyra suffered under the persecution of Diocletian at the beginning of the fourth century. An innkeeper by trade, he used his house and his means to shelter persecuted Christians, to care for prisoners, and to give burial to the bodies of the martyrs when it was forbidden. For this holy boldness he was himself seized, tortured, and beheaded.

The Church remembers in him a layman whose ordinary trade became a ministry of mercy, and whose mercy became martyrdom. He is commemorated on June 7.
6-7.name: Theodotus of Ancyra

6-7.bio:
Saint Potamiaena was a Christian slave of Alexandria of great beauty and purity. Refusing her master's advances and denounced as a Christian, she was tortured and, tradition relates, slowly lowered into boiling pitch in the early third century.

The soldier Basilides who led her to execution treated her with kindness; she promised to pray for him, and shortly afterwards he confessed Christ and was beheaded. Their story is told by Eusebius.
6-7.desc: Holy Virgin Martyr Potamiaena of Alexandria, and the soldier Basilides who was converted by her.
6-7.name: Potamiaena of Alexandria and Basilides

6-7.bio:
Saint Panagis Basias was born in Lixouri on Kefalonia in 1801, received a good education and became a priest and teacher. He gave himself to the poor and to prayer, and in his later years took upon himself the foolishness for Christ, through which he was granted gifts of discernment and healing.

He reposed in 1888 and was glorified by the Ecumenical Patriarchate in 1986. He is greatly loved on Kefalonia, where many bear his name.
6-7.desc: Venerable Panagis (Paisios) Basias of Lixouri, Kefalonia, priest and fool for Christ of the nineteenth century.
6-7.name: Panagis Basias of Kefalonia

6-7.bio: Saint Zenais lived in Caesarea in Palestine and is remembered in the synaxaria as a wonderworker who healed the sick through her prayers. Tradition relates that she gave her life for Christ during the persecutions of the third century.
6-7.desc: Holy Zenais of Caesarea in Palestine, a wonderworker of the early Church.
6-7.name: Zenais the Wonderworker

6-7.bio:
Saint Anastasios Gordios was born in the village of Vraniana in the Agrapha mountains in 1654 and studied under Eugenios Giannoulis. He became a priest-monk and spent his life teaching, writing and guiding the people of the mountains during the Ottoman period.

He reposed in 1729 and was numbered among the saints by the Ecumenical Patriarchate. He is honoured as one of the teachers who kept faith and letters alive among the Greeks.
6-7.desc: Venerable Anastasios Gordios of Vraniana in Agrapha, priest-monk and teacher of the enslaved Greek nation.
6-7.name: Anastasios Gordios

6-7.bio: Saints Aesia and Susanna were virgins of Caesarea in Palestine who, tradition relates, were disciples of the hieromartyr Pamphilus. They confessed Christ during the persecution and were put to death, and the synaxaria honour them together on this day.
6-7.desc: Holy Virgin Martyrs Aesia and Susanna of Caesarea in Palestine.
6-7.name: Aesia and Susanna, Martyrs

6-7.bio: Saint Lykarion was a young Christian of Egypt who, tradition relates, was arrested for his faith, endured torture and was finally beheaded, receiving the crown of martyrdom.
6-7.desc: Holy Martyr Lykarion of Egypt, who suffered for Christ in his youth.
6-7.name: Lykarion the Martyr

6-8.bio:
The Holy Great Martyr Theodore Stratelates, the Commander, was a military governor in Asia Minor who suffered for Christ under the emperor Licinius at the beginning of the fourth century. Confessing the Lord openly and overturning the worship of idols, he endured cruel tortures and was beheaded, encouraging the faithful to stand firm.

On June 8 the Church commemorates the translation of his relics to his family home at Euchaita, according to his own dying wish. With St. Theodore the Recruit he is one of the two beloved warrior saints named Theodore, invoked by soldiers and honored throughout the Orthodox world.
6-8.desc: Translation of relics of Theodore Stratelates.
6-8.name: Theodore Stratelates

6-8.bio:
Saint Kalliope was a Christian maiden of great beauty who, during the persecution under Decius in the third century, refused both marriage to a pagan and the renunciation of her faith. Tradition relates that she was cruelly tortured and finally beheaded.

Her name is widespread among Greek women, who keep their name day on this feast.
6-8.desc: Holy Virgin Martyr Kalliope, who suffered for Christ in the third century.
6-8.name: Kalliope the Martyr

6-8.bio: Saint Theophanes was a Christian of Constantinople who, tradition relates, as a boy was taken and made a Muslim, but later returned to the Christian faith. When this became known he was tortured and finally executed in 1559, receiving the crown of martyrdom.
6-8.desc: New Martyr Theophanes of Constantinople, who suffered in 1559 after returning to the faith of Christ.
6-8.name: Theophanes the New Martyr

6-8.bio: Saints Nicander and Marcian were soldiers who refused to sacrifice to idols when the imperial edict was published. Tradition relates that they were beheaded together, Marcian encouraged by his wife who stood by him to the end. They suffered in the early fourth century at Durostorum on the Danube.
6-8.desc: Holy Martyrs Nicander and Marcian, soldiers beheaded for Christ at Durostorum.
6-8.name: Nicander and Marcian, Martyrs

6-8.bio:
Saint Naukratios was the second son of Basil the Elder and Saint Emmelia, and a brother of Saints Basil the Great, Gregory of Nyssa and Macrina. Gifted as an orator, he abandoned a worldly career at about twenty-one and withdrew to the family estate in Pontus, where he lived as an ascetic and cared for the poor.

He died suddenly, around the year 357, while hunting to feed those in his care. His family's grief and the strength of his sister Macrina are described by Saint Gregory of Nyssa.
6-8.desc: Venerable Naukratios, brother of Saint Basil the Great, who lived as an ascetic in Pontus and died young.
6-8.name: Naukratios, Brother of Basil the Great

6-8.bio: Saint Paul was a monk of the monastery of Kaiouma in Constantinople during the iconoclast persecution. Tradition relates that for his defence of the holy icons he was tortured and burned, and the Church honours him as a confessor.
6-8.desc: Venerable Paul the Confessor of the monastery of Kaiouma, who suffered for the holy icons.
6-8.name: Paul the Confessor of Kaiouma

6-8.bio: Saint Theodore was a Greek by birth who came to Russia with the first missionaries after the baptism of Prince Vladimir and became the first bishop of Rostov in the early eleventh century. He laboured to convert the pagan population of the region and reposed in Suzdal.
6-8.desc: Saint Theodore, first Bishop of Rostov and Suzdal, missionary among the pagans of northern Russia.
6-8.name: Theodore of Rostov

6-9.bio:
St. Cyril was Archbishop of Alexandria in the fifth century and one of the great theologians of the Church. When Nestorius denied that the Virgin Mary may be called Theotokos, Birth-Giver of God, Cyril rose in defense of the truth that the one born of her is truly God the Word made flesh. He presided at the Third Ecumenical Council at Ephesus in 431, which upheld the Orthodox faith.

Called the Pillar of Orthodoxy, he reposed in 444, leaving writings that remain foundations of the Church's teaching on Christ. He is commemorated on June 9, and with St. Athanasios on January 18.
6-9.desc: St. Cyril, Archbishop of Alexandria, Pillar of Orthodoxy.
6-9.name: Cyril, Archbishop of Alexandria

6-9.bio: These five consecrated virgins lived in Persia during the persecution of Christians under King Shapur II in the fourth century. Denounced by a priest who had renounced the faith, they refused to worship the sun and, tradition relates, were beheaded by him at the king's command.
6-9.desc: Holy Five Virgin Martyrs Thecla, Mariamne, Martha, Mary and Ennatha, beheaded in Persia under Shapur II.
6-9.greek: Θέκλα, Μαριάμνη, Μάρθα, Μαρία και Ενναθά
6-9.name: Thecla, Mariamne, Martha, Mary and Ennatha, Virgin Martyrs of Persia

6-9.bio: Saint Alexander was bishop of Prusa in Bithynia. Tradition relates that he was arrested during the persecutions for confessing Christ, endured torture and was beheaded, receiving the crown of martyrdom.
6-9.desc: Hieromartyr Alexander, Bishop of Prusa in Bithynia, beheaded for Christ.
6-9.name: Alexander of Prusa

6-9.bio:
Saint Cyril was born in Moscow in 1337 and became a monk of the Simonov monastery, where he knew Saint Sergius of Radonezh. Guided, tradition relates, by a vision of the Theotokos, he went north to the shore of White Lake and founded the monastery that bears his name.

He was renowned for humility, strict community life and gifts of prophecy and healing, and he reposed in 1427. His monastery became one of the greatest in Russia.
6-9.desc: Venerable Cyril, founder and abbot of the monastery of White Lake (Belozersk), a great father of Russian monasticism.
6-9.greek: Κύριλλος ο εν τη Λευκή Λίμνη
6-9.name: Cyril of White Lake

6-9.bio:
Saint Columba was born in Ireland of a noble family in 521 and became a monk and founder of monasteries. In 563 he left Ireland with twelve companions and settled on the island of Iona, from which he preached to the Picts of Scotland and established a monastic community that shaped the Church of the British Isles.

He reposed at Iona in 597, and the accounts of his life record his gifts of prophecy and many miracles.
6-9.desc: Venerable Columba, abbot of Iona and enlightener of Scotland.
6-9.name: Columba of Iona

6-9.bio: Saint Alexander was a monk of the Savior-Stone monastery on Lake Kubensk who withdrew to the river Kushta in the forests of Vologda and founded a monastery there in the fifteenth century. He was known for his humility and love of solitude, and reposed in 1439.
6-9.desc: Venerable Alexander, abbot of Kushta in Vologda, a hermit of the Russian north.
6-9.name: Alexander of Kushta
